commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 (PR #1300): removes hard-coded exemplar entry_is_line_a..e derived rules (proof atoms citing other chapters' HTS lines) from every generated chapter and makes them caller inputs; summary claims runtime semantics unchanged — unsure, part of the same decoupling repair.
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: Chapter 20 (preparations of vegetables, fruit and nuts) derived entry_is_line_a..e from five out-of-chapter HTS statistical reporting numbers with proof atoms citing other chapters' provisions, so the trade-action components gated on those flags rested on conditions with no basis in this chapter's cited source.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 12; diff read individually and normalized-compared — only placement-gate cosmetics (10 parenthesis pairs, `effective_from`) differ. Same caveats as index 12.
triage.verifier_justification: The ch13 diff deletes five `kind: derived` rules whose formulas were identity tests on statistical reporting numbers from other chapters (7202.11.10.00 ferroalloys, 7601.10.30.00 aluminum, 9506.62.40.40 footballs, 2203.00.00.30 beer, 8541.42.00.10 PV cells), each carrying proof atoms citing those other chapters' provisions; the chapter 13 module cites no chapter-13 HTS provision at all (zero `us/statute/hts/13*` citation paths in the post file), so those conditions had no basis in this chapter's own source. Because chapter/line routing happens in entry preparation ("Chapter and rate-line routing occur in entry preparation, never through cross-chapter RuleSpec dispatch"), the flags were identically false for any chapter-13 entry, which forced `section_301_component_rate` (all five gated terms), the §232 aluminum/beer basis flag, §201, §338 and the §122 exclusion branches to a fixed outcome no chapter-13 line could escape. This is a change to encoded meaning, not provenance: derived formulas are removed and the identifiers become unconstrained caller inputs, so the module's input surface and runtime values change, and the removal is exactly the "condition with no basis in the cited source / grounded on the wrong provision" case. I hold confidence at 0.68 rather than higher because this commit only removes the ungrounded definitions without supplying a source-grounded replacement inside the module, and the repair is incomplete in the same file.

triage.verifier_notes:
inferred from verified sibling module index 12 (same kind and rule path in this chunk). Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "mechanical" does not hold — five derived rules with formulas are deleted and the identifiers become implicit caller inputs under the "referenced-implies-input convention", so inputs and runtime values change, not just hashes/excerpts/metadata; (2) "not_a_defect / architecture-only" is weakened by the PR body's own fidelity finding that the witness's exemplar coupling "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins"; (3) "wrong_entity_or_scope" is a worse fit than untraceable_branch, since the entity (CustomsEntry) is right and the defect is conditions grounded on provisions from other chapters, which the untraceable_branch definition explicitly covers.

Caveats for the reviewer: (a) the repair is incomplete in this same file — post-fix ch13 still contains `- name: entry_is_energy_resource` with `formula: (((((((hts_number == "7202.11.10.00")))))))` and proof atoms citing `us/statute/hts/7202` ("Ferroalloys:"), i.e. one hard-coded out-of-chapter exemplar identity test survives at post line ~1950; (b) every referencing formula is byte-identical across this diff (e.g. `section_301_component_rate` still sums `if entry_is_line_a and origin_is_china: ...` through `entry_is_line_e`), so the membership-semantic re-gating described in the PR body lands in other commits of PR #1300, not here; (c) the module summary retains the boilerplate sentence "This deterministic RuleSpec serialization changes no formula tokens, dates, inputs, proof atoms, or runtime values", which is false for this commit — the flags stop being always-false constants for this chapter; (d) the file is `module.kind: composition` (generated, assembled rather than encoder-produced), which is the main reason a reviewer might downgrade this to "unclear"; it is still a rulespec/v1 module containing rule formulas, so not_a_rule_module does not apply.
